title: Supporting himself by gambling; third-grade schooling
summary: Records did not pay, so gambling supported his family; he left school after third grade at Arthur P. Williams School.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Wasco, no. I really don't. No. So all through this period, when you were recording, you obviously weren't making that much money off your records, so how were you supporting yourself? Through your gigs or playing? Doing your gambling? Doing your gambling.
Doing your gambling, you know. That was your real, your sole support?
Well, I had to eat, I had to sleep, I had to pay rent, my children had to continually go to school.

Yeah. I was doing the suffering, you know, because I had to see that they make it, you know. How far did you get in school? Really, I didn't go to school. I went to school in third grade. That was on? That was on, Perdita and. Yeah, it was a downtown school.
Yeah, Liberty I think. Perdita and Liberty. Yeah. They took up the whole block as well, you see. From Liberty to Franklin.
So it seems that most of the time your music didn't really support you. I mean all the records you were doing.

No, really. I wasn't making a living off of the music, just a help, you know. Other than sessions I would play a little gig sometimes with different fellas, and after the gig, if there wasn't no gig, well I knew where my spot was. And that was back on the corner with those chords, you know.
